To determine whether graft success, corneal endothelial cell loss (ECL), and morphometric changes 1 year after DMEK are associated with cornea donor diabetes severity measured by severity score, donor's postmortem level of hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and postmortem advanced glycation end products (AGEs) or advanced oxidation end products (AOPs).

Design, setting, and participants

This was a secondary analysis of a multicenter, double-masked, randomized clinical trial at 28 clinical sites (46 surgeons) and 13 eye banks in the US among individuals undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of donors. Data analysis was conducted from September 1, 2025, through April 30, 2026.

Intervention

DMEK performed with a cornea from a donor without or with diabetes, assigned using a minimization procedure (comparable to randomization) to achieve an approximate 2:1 distribution, respectively.

Main outcomes and measures

Graft success, ECL, coefficient of variation (CV) of cell area, and percentage of hexagonal cells (HEX) at 1 year from eye bank and postoperative specular central endothelial images.

Results

A total of 1097 individuals (1421 study eyes; median [IQR] age, 71 [66-76] years; 631 [57.5%] female) undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK (1044 [95.2%] for Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy) were included. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of 472 donors (542 study donor corneas). Among 968 eyes with a postmortem donor HbA1c level lower than 6.5%, the 1-year graft success rate was 97.1% (95% CI, 95.4%-98.4%), compared with 97.4% (95% CI, 93.9%-100.0%), 93.0% (95% CI, 83.3%-98.8%), and 95.8% (95% CI, 87.3%-100.0%) among eyes with a donor HbA1c level of 6.5% to less than 7.5% (n = 194), 7.5% to less than 9.0% (n = 86), and 9.0% or higher (n = 48), respectively (P = .72). There was no significant difference in mean ECD across donor HbA1c groups. Donor diabetes severity measured with severity score, donor HbA1c level, and AGE and AOP metrics was not associated with 1-year graft failure, ECD, CV in cell area, or HEX percentage.

Conclusions and relevance

This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial found that ECL and morphometry 1 year after DMEK were not affected by cornea donor diabetes severity. Comparable 1-year graft success, ECL, and cell morphometrics with tissue from donors with and without diabetes, regardless of the diabetes severity biomarker values observed, support the use of corneas from donors with diabetes for endothelial keratoplasty procedures without additional preoperative testing or risk stratification based on the diabetes status of the cornea donor.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05134480.

records.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.

content.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate long-term trends in treated dry eye disease (DED) prevalence and medication prescribing patterns in Korea using a nationwide mandatory insurance claims database.

Design

Retrospective nationwide clinical cohort study.

Participants

Patients identified from the Korean NHIS mandatory claims database (2014-2023).

Methods

DED was defined by at least one relevant ICD-10 diagnosis code together with at least one prescription for a DED-related topical medication within the same calendar year. Annual overall, sex-specific, and age-specific prevalence was calculated using the corresponding mid-year resident population. Medication classes and single-use versus multi-use formulations were evaluated. Medication use in Sjögren syndrome-associated versus non-Sjögren DED was compared using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and sex.

Main outcome measures

Annual treated DED prevalence, medication prescribing proportions, formulation-specific prescribing trends, and differences between Sjögren syndrome-associated and non-Sjögren syndrome DED.

Results

Approximately 61.8 million patient-years were analyzed, representing 9.87 million unique patients. Annual treated DED prevalence ranged from 4.84% to 5.61% and was consistently higher in women and older individuals. Hyaluronic acid (HA) remained the most prescribed medication, although its proportional share declined from 85.03% in 2014 to 76.89% in 2023 (P < .001). Diquafosol prescriptions increased from 4.61% to 10.77%, and cyclosporine prescriptions increased from 2.39% to 5.77% (both P < .001). Single-use HA prescriptions increased from 39.73% to 73.76% (P < .001), and single-use diquafosol accounted for 61.8% of diquafosol prescriptions by 2023. Cyclosporine was prescribed to 26.00% of patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED and 7.51% of those with non-Sjögren DED; the adjusted OR was 4.06 (95% CI, 3.99-4.12).

Conclusions

Over the past decade, DED management in Korea shifted toward the anti-inflammatory cyclosporine, the mucin and water secretagogue diquafosol, and preservative-free single-use formulations. Patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED demonstrated distinct prescribing patterns, including substantially greater cyclosporine use after adjustment for age and sex.

records.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.

content.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To prospectively validate the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS), a standardized slit-lamp grading tool, by evaluating associations with objective corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and visual acuity in a real-world cystinosis cohort.

Design

Prospective observational cross-sectional study.

Participants

Seventy patients (140 eyes) with confirmed cystinosis were examined at the 2024-2025 Cystinosis Research Foundation Day of Hope Clinics.

Methods

All eyes underwent live slit-lamp UCI CCCS grading (0-5). Pentacam Scheimpflug densitometry was obtained in 68 eyes. Two ophthalmologists independently graded patients during the 2025 clinic to assess inter-rater reliability. Patient-reported symptoms, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and topical cysteamine treatment data were collected. Linear mixed-effects models accounting for within-patient correlation were used for densitometry and BCVA analyses. Symptom associations were evaluated at the patient level using Kendall's tau-b.

Main outcome measures

Inter-rater reliability of UCI CCCS; associations with corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and BCVA.

Results

Inter-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.995; 95% CI, 0.992-0.996). Linear mixed-effects modeling demonstrated significant associations between UCI CCCS grade and central (p = 0.0016) and anterior corneal densitometry (p = 0.0011) after accounting for within-patient correlation between fellow eyes. Higher UCI CCCS grades were significantly associated with greater photophobia (τ = 0.397, p < 0.0001), foreign-body sensation (τ = 0.295, p = 0.0047), and ocular dryness (τ = 0.405, p = 0.0001). No statistically significant association was observed between UCI CCCS grade and BCVA after accounting for within-patient correlation (p = 0.4389). No significant differences in UCI CCCS or corneal densitometry were observed across topical cysteamine treatment groups.

Conclusion

The UCI CCCS is a highly reproducible, clinically practical grading tool associated with objective corneal densitometry and patient-reported symptom burden, while BCVA was not significantly associated with UCI CCCS grade. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate treatment responsiveness and prognostic value.

records.title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis: Outcomes After Descemet Membrane Endothelial Keratoplasty Versus Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty.

content.title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis: Outcomes After Descemet Membrane Endothelial Keratoplasty Versus Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of ultrathin Descemet stripping (automated) endothelial keratoplasty (UT-DS(A)EK) versus Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) for the treatment of Fuchs endothelial dystrophy (FED) and bullous keratopathy (BK).

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

Literature containing DMEK and UT-DSAEK were searched in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, PubMed, EMBASE, LILACS, and through manual reference searching. Studies were included that measured the outcome of interventions-including best corrected visual acuity (BCVA), endothelial cell density (ECD), and postoperative complications, especially graft detachment with the need of re-bubbling, graft rejection, graft failure, and postoperative elevated intraocular pressure (IOP)-in patients with FED and BK. Included outcomes were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMD) or risk ratios (RR) using random effects models. Inter-study heterogeneity was assessed using the Q-test and I2 statistic.

Results

Seven (of 163) studies met all the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Meta-analysis showed a significantly better BCVA 12 months postoperatively, but an increased re-bubbling rate in eyes after DMEK compared with eyes after UT-DS(A)EK (BCVA: SMD = 0.50 [95% CI 0.27-0.74] and re-bubbling rate: RR = 0.33 [95% CI 0.16-0.67]). All other parameters did not differ significantly between both interventions, although estimates were imprecise (graft failure: RR = 0.65 [95% CI 0.18-2.30], graft rejection: RR = 1.40 [95% CI 0.27-7.30], and postoperative intraocular pressure elevation: RR = 1.14 [95% CI 0.60-2.18]). Postoperative SMDs of ECD could not be evaluated due to significant heterogeneity between studies.

Conclusions

Although the improvement in BCVA was higher after UT-DS(A)EK than after conventional DS(A)EK, the BCVA after DMEK was still superior. The complication rates were comparable for both procedures, except for the higher rate of re-bubbling after DMEK.

records.title: Efficacy of Thin and Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty and Influence of Graft Thickness on Postoperative Outcomes: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy of Thin and Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty and Influence of Graft Thickness on Postoperative Outcomes: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of thin and ultrathin Descemet stripping automated endothelial keratoplasty (T-DSAEK and UT-DSAEK, with graft thickness <130 and <100 µm, respectively), depending on graft thickness.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Method

PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ScienceDirect databases were searched until October 1, 2021. We computed random-effect meta-analysis on postoperative outcomes of T/UT-DSAEK, stratified by graft thickness (<80 μm, 80-100 μm, and 100-130 μm). The main postoperative outcome was visual acuity (logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution [logMAR]). Secondary outcomes were pachymetry (μm), endothelial cell count (cell/mm2), spherical equivalent (diopter [D]), rebubbling rate (%), and rejection rate (%). Meta-regressions compared postoperative outcomes depending on graft thickness and search for putative confusion factors.

Results

We included 47 articles for a total of 2141 eyes of 2040 patients. T/UT-DSAEK globally improved visual acuity (effect size = -0.38 logMAR [95% confidence interval {CI} -0.46 to -0.30 logMAR]), without difference depending on graft thickness. Overall, pachymetry improved (-60.6 µm [95% CI -101 to -19.7 µm]), endothelial cell count decreased (-1039 cells/mm2 [95% CI -1209 to -868 cells/mm2), spherical equivalent resulted in a hyperopic shift (0.74 D [95% CI -0.50 to 1.97 D), the graft rejection rate was 0.2% (95% CI -0.1% to 0.4%), and the rebubbling rate was 8.7% (95% CI 6.8%-10.5%). Grafts >100 μm induced a hyperopic shift. Metaregressions did not demonstrate differences between the 3 groups (<80 μm, 80-100 μm, or 100-130 μm) in any outcomes.

Conclusion

All T/UT-DSAEK thickness groups provided similar visual acuity, pachymetry, endothelial cell count, rejection rate, and rebubbling rate regardless of graft thickness. A hyperopic shift was induced by grafts >100 μm.

records.title: Glands of Moll: history, current knowledge and their role in ocular surface homeostasis and disease.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Glands of Moll: history, current knowledge and their role in ocular surface homeostasis and disease.
content.abstract: Over the last 20 years, research into the Meibomian glands of the eyelids has increased exponentially and is now widely recognized as a field of research. It is all the more astonishing that knowledge about another type of gland in the eyelids, the Moll glands or ciliary glands, has almost stagnated and there has been little to almost no progress, even though this type of gland as a whole takes up a relatively large volume in the upper and lower eyelids. There is not much information about the namesake Moll or the function of the glands although these are listed in nearly every textbook of anatomy, histology and ophthalmology. For this reason, we set out to compile the existing knowledge about the Moll glands of the eyelids in order to create a basis for follow-up studies and to stimulate research into this type of gland. In our literature research, we went back to the middle of the 19th century and made contact with a descendant of the Moll family and illustrate their relevance for the present. The structure of the secretory part of the Moll glands is very well described, a number of secretory products are known, but the current state of research allows only very rough speculations about their function. The overview provides numerous interesting insights, which, however, raise more questions than they provide answers.

records.title: The role of CFTR in the eye, and the effect of early highly effective modulator treatment for cystic fibrosis on eye health.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The role of CFTR in the eye, and the effect of early highly effective modulator treatment for cystic fibrosis on eye health.
content.abstract: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) is a protein that plays a crucial role in various human organs, including the respiratory and digestive systems. Dysfunctional CFTR is the key variant of the lethal genetic disorder, cystic fibrosis (CF). In the past decade, highly effective CFTR modulator therapies, including elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor, have revolutionised CF management by correcting the underlying molecular defect to improve patient outcomes and life expectancy. Despite demonstrating multiorgan efficacy, clinical studies have largely overlooked the potential for ocular disturbances with CFTR modulator therapy, with the exception of a few case studies reporting the presence of crystalline lens pathologies in young children on CFTR modulators, and in breastfed infants born to individuals who were on CFTR modulator treatment during pregnancy. CFTR is present in multiple tissues during embryonic development, including the eye, and its expression can be influenced by genetic and environmental factors. This review summarises the role of CFTR in the eye, and the potential impact of CFTR on eye function and vision later in life. This information provides a framework for understanding the use and possible effects of CFTR-modulating therapeutics in the context of eye health, including the potential to leverage the eye for non-invasive and accessible diagnostic and monitoring capabilities in patients with CF.

records.title: Health-Related Quality-of-Life Outcomes for Upper Blepharoplasty and Blepharoptosis Surgery: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Health-Related Quality-of-Life Outcomes for Upper Blepharoplasty and Blepharoptosis Surgery: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To review the literature and identify the health-related quality-of-life (HRQL) outcomes that used a validated instrument in the assessment of upper blepharoplasty, blepharoptosis surgery, or combination surgery.

Methods

A literature search was last conducted in the PubMed database in January 2025 to identify all studies in the English language investigating HRQL outcomes that used a validated instrument in the assessment of upper blepharoplasty, blepharoptosis surgery, or combination surgery. The literature search yielded 773 citations, and 20 studies met the inclusion criteria. All studies included a validated instrument to assess HRQL. A panel methodologist then assigned a level of evidence rating for each study that met the inclusion criteria.

Results

Three studies were rated level I, 8 studies were rated level II, and 9 studies were rated level III. The surgeries performed in the studies included upper blepharoplasty, blepharoptosis correction, or both. Some studies also included the addition of brow ptosis repair. Seven studies focused on the effect of the upper eyelid interventions on dry eye symptoms, 5 of which observed no subjective worsening and 1 of which demonstrated symptoms that were transient. The remaining studies focused on aspects of visual function, patient satisfaction, self-consciousness of appearance, benefit in daily life, ocular symptoms, headache symptoms, or a combination thereof and found a benefit of surgery in these various domains. Three studies that examined the long-term HRQL benefit of blepharoptosis correction noted continued improvement at mean follow-up intervals ranging from 1.5 years to 3.6 years after surgery.

Conclusions

Most HRQL studies examining the effects of upper blepharoplasty, blepharoptosis correction, or both on dry eye symptoms found no significant worsening of subjective metrics. Other studies demonstrated that surgery could provide improved HRQL outcomes that persist for several years.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

records.title: A comprehensive scoping review of methodological approaches and clinical applications of tear fluid biomarkers.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: A comprehensive scoping review of methodological approaches and clinical applications of tear fluid biomarkers.
content.abstract: Tear fluid is an emerging source of disease biomarkers, drawing attention due to its quick, inexpensive, and non-invasive collection. The advancements in detection techniques enable the measurement of ultra-low biomarker levels from small sample volumes typical of tear fluid. The lack of standardized protocols for collection, processing, and analysis of tear fluid remains a significant challenge. To address this, we convened the Tear Research Network Review Taskforce in 2022 to review protocols from the past three decades, providing a comprehensive overview of the methodologies used in tear fluid biomarker research. A total of 1484 articles published from January 1974 to May 2024 from two electronic databases, Embase and Ovid MEDLINE, were reviewed. An exponential increase in the number of articles on tear fluid biomarkers was observed from 2015 onwards. The two most commonly reported collection methods were; glass capillaries (45.2%), and Schirmer's strips (25%), with glass capillary tube collection remaining the most frequent method until 2019, when Schirmer's strips became the leading method. Most articles analyzed tear fluid proteins (65%) and focused on a single analyte (32.3%). In recent years, an increase was observed in the type and number of examined analytes. The differences in the reported methodologies and protocols underscore the need for standardization and harmonization within the field of tear fluid biomarkers to minimize methodological differences and reduce variability in clinical outcomes. Consistent and detailed reporting is essential for improving the reproducibility and validity of tear fluid studies, in order to advance their potential clinical applications.

records.title: Efficacy of Amniotic Membrane Grafting for the Treatment of Chemical and Thermal Ocular Surface Injuries: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Efficacy of Amniotic Membrane Grafting for the Treatment of Chemical and Thermal Ocular Surface Injuries: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Objective

To evaluate the published literature on the efficacy of amniotic membrane grafting (AMG) in the management of acute chemical and thermal ocular surface burns with respect to the rate of corneal re-epithelialization and improvement of visual acuity or corneal clarity.

Methods

Literature searches were conducted in the PubMed database in May 2023 and updated in January 2024 and were limited to the English language without date restrictions. The searches yielded 474 citations; 58 were reviewed in full text, and 9 met the inclusion criteria. Four studies were rated level II, and 5 studies were rated level III. This assessment focuses on 3 level II articles that provided consistent primary and secondary outcomes but demonstrated suboptimal study design with respect to power calculations and lacked a priori sample-size calculations.

Results

Amniotic membrane grafting significantly improved corneal re-epithelialization compared with medical therapy alone in eyes with moderate-grade burns. For severely burned eyes, AMG demonstrated no advantage over medical therapy. Additionally, AMG demonstrated no significant advantage over medical therapy for improved visual acuity or corneal clarity for moderate or severe ocular surface burns.

Conclusions

The best available level II evidence suggests that AMG in the setting of acute ocular surface burns has efficacy in hastening re-epithelialization in moderate burns. As an adjuvant to medical therapy, it did not demonstrate a benefit in improving re-epithelialization in severe burns or visual acuity or corneal clarity in either moderate or severe burns.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found after the references.

records.title: Unravelling CYP4V2: Clinical features, genetic insights, pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic strategies in Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Unravelling CYP4V2: Clinical features, genetic insights, pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic strategies in Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy.
content.abstract: Inherited retinal dystrophies (IRDs) comprise a spectrum of disease phenotypes with genetic heterogeneity and clinical phenotypic diversity. Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy (BCD) represents a distinct IRD subtype characterized by crystalline deposits in the retina. Although rare in Western populations, BCD ranks among the most prevalent IRDs in East Asia, affecting an estimated 124,000 to 377,000 individuals worldwide. As a severe type of IRD, BCD demonstrates accelerated progression and currently lacks effective treatment. The BCD disease is caused by a biallelic mutation in the CYP4V2 gene. With a coding sequence (CDS) of 1,578 bp, CYP4V2 can be effectively encapsulated into adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors. As a hydroxylase, CYP4V2 is mainly expressed in retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells, which can be transduced by AAVs and are suitable for gene augmentation therapy that replaces the function of mutant proteins. Given the large patient population, severe visual impairment, and feasibility of gene therapy, several research groups are interested in developing gene therapy products for BCD, and two products entering Phase III clinical trials have made significant progress. This review outlines the clinical features, genetic insights and pathogenic mechanisms of BCD and discusses the ongoing gene therapy clinical trials, including efficacy and concerns. This knowledge will help us bridge the gap between molecular studies and clinical treatments, facilitating translation from bench to bedside. We believe that advancements in BCD gene therapy will inform the treatment of other IRDs.

records.title: Beyond convolutions and supervised learning with transformers and representation learning for retinal image analysis.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Beyond convolutions and supervised learning with transformers and representation learning for retinal image analysis.
content.abstract: Retinal image analysis has enjoyed groundbreaking advances in the last ten years due to seismic improvements in image analysis techniques from the field of computer vision. Previous reviews in deep learning and artificial intelligence (AI) (Schmidt-Erfurth et al., 2018; Ting et al., 2019) have either focused on supervised learning, where labels are curated or manually created, or concentrated on the application of AI in specific image modalities and retina diseases (Hormel et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024a (Hormel et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024a)). In this review, we sought to summarize the advances in the field with the shift towards label-free approaches using representational learning and the emergence of vision transformers as alternatives to convolutional neural networks for image analysis. These advances include semi-supervised learning, self-supervised learning and directly led to the advent of foundation models, vision-language models, and multi-modal models.

records.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.

content.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.
content.abstract:
Importance

Gene expression profiling (GEP) reliably predicts metastatic uveal melanoma risk and is used to manage uveal melanoma (UM) in patients with this diagnosis. Efforts to refine molecular prognostication continue.

Objective

To determine if confirmatory cytopathology findings influence the prognostic accuracy of a commercially available GEP/Preferentially Expressed Antigen in Melanoma (PRAME) assay.

Design, setting, and participants

The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group 2 study, a prospective cohort study, was conducted from 2017 to 2020 with follow-up recorded at 6-month intervals. This was a multicenter study that included patients with choroidal and/or ciliary body melanoma and results from a 15-GEP and PRAME RNA expression (15-GEP/PRAME) assay. Patients with iris tumors or less than 6 months' follow-up were excluded. Study data were analyzed from April 2025 to July 2026.

Exposures

15-GEP/PRAME, cytopathology, and next-generation sequencing (NGS).

Main outcomes and measures

Metastatic uveal melanoma rates in patients who had 15-GEP/PRAME and confirmatory cytopathology (CCP) results confirming or suspicious for UM (GEP+CCP) were compared with those who had 15-GEP/PRAME and no cytopathology performed, or unknown or nondiagnostic cytopathology results (GEP only). UM-associated variants identified by NGS were also evaluated.

Results

Of 1537 patients (mean [SD] age, 62.0 [13.4] years; 787 male [51.2%]), 727 (47.3%) had CCP results, and 810 (52.7%) had nondiagnostic cytopathology results or no cytopathology performed. Class 2/PRAME+ tumors were more common (136 of 727 [18.7%]) in the GEP+CCP group than in the GEP-only group (72 of 810 [8.9%]; 9.8% difference; 95% CI, 6.4-13.3; P <.001), whereas class 1/PRAME- tumors were less common (330 of 727 [45.4%] vs 495 of 810 [61.1%]; 15.7% difference; 95% CI, 10.8-20.6; P <.001). In patients with GEP+CCP, 22.7% (n = 165) developed metastasis vs 15.4% (n = 125) in patients with GEP only (7.3% difference, 95% CI, 3.3-11.2; P < .001). Adjusting for 15-GEP/PRAME status, there were no differences in metastasis rates between CCP groups. Of 1327 patients with successful NGS, 94.1% (605 of 643) in the GEP+CCP group and 71.9% (492 of 684) in the GEP-only group had a UM-associated variant (22.2% difference, 95% CI, 18.3-26.0; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cohort study reveal that no differences in metastasis outcomes were observed between patients with and without CCP within any GEP/PRAME categories. UM-associated variants were found less frequently in the GEP-only group than in the GEP+CCP group. In this cohort, 15-GEP/PRAME classification without CCP retained prognostic validity, supporting its clinical consideration in guiding metastatic surveillance in cases in which cytopathology is unavailable.

records.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.

content.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Investigate the structure-function relationships between epiretinal membrane (ERM) stage, tractional abnormalities, and the gap area between the ERM and the retinal surface, in relation to visual acuity and quantitative contrast sensitivity function in patients with idiopathic epiretinal membrane.

Methods

This was a retrospective, cross-sectional study involving 111 participants diagnosed with idiopathic ERM. All patients underwent a comprehensive ophthalmologic examination, spectral-domain optical coherence tomography imaging using the SPECTRALIS Heidelberg system, and contrast sensitivity (CS) testing using the quantitative contrast sensitivity function method.

Results

Progressive stages of ERM were associated with declines in both CS and visual acuity (β* = -0.45 to -0.19, P < 0.02), with CS showing a more pronounced reduction than visual acuity, especially between controls and Stage 1. Ectopic inner foveal layer thickness exhibited a similar pattern of decline in both visual acuity (β* = 0.42, P < 0.001) and CS (β* = -0.46 to -0.18, all P < 0.02). By contrast, SUKIMA showed no significant association with any of the visual measurements assessed. Among the tractional abnormalities, the cotton ball sign correlated with diminished vision, particularly reflected by a notable drop in CS at the highest spatial frequencies tested with reduced CS at 12 cycles per degree (β* = -0.44, P = 0.02) and 18 cycles per degree (β* = -0.46, P = 0.02).

Conclusion

Quantitative contrast sensitivity function testing is particularly important for assessing visual function in ERM development, especially in the early stages.

records.title: Longitudinal Changes in Scleral Thickness after Half-dose Photodynamic Therapy in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.

content.title: Longitudinal Changes in Scleral Thickness after Half-dose Photodynamic Therapy in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate longitudinal changes in scleral thickness after half-dose photodynamic therapy (PDT) in eyes with central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) in parallel with widefield assessment of choroidal thickness.

Methods

This retrospective observational study included 41 eyes of 41 patients with unilateral CSC who underwent half-dose PDT for persistent subretinal fluid and completed 12 months of follow-up. Scleral thickness was measured in 4 quadrants using anterior-segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) at baseline and at 3 and 12 months after PDT. Widefield choroidal thickness was assessed using widefield swept-source OCT with an 18-mm grid divided into 9 sectors. Untreated fellow eyes served as a reference group.

Results

In treated eyes, widefield choroidal thickness decreased significantly at 3 months after PDT across all 9 predefined sectors (all P < 0.05) and remained reduced at 12 months, with no significant differences between 3 and 12 months. In untreated fellow eyes, no consistent longitudinal changes in choroidal thickness were observed; however, a statistically significant reduction was noted only in the outer superonasal sector at 3 months (P = 0.015). In contrast, scleral thickness showed no significant changes at any time point in either treated or fellow eyes (all P > 0.05).

Conclusions

Despite widespread and sustained choroidal thinning after half-dose PDT, scleral thickness remained unchanged for at least 12 months in eyes with CSC. These findings suggest that scleral thickening in CSC is unlikely to represent a readily reversible response to treatment-associated choroidal changes and may instead reflect a relatively stable anatomical feature.

records.title: Structure and function of ABCA4 and its role in the visual cycle and Stargardt macular degeneration.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Structure and function of ABCA4 and its role in the visual cycle and Stargardt macular degeneration.
content.abstract: ABCA4 is a member of the superfamily of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters that is preferentially localized along the rim region of rod and cone photoreceptor outer segment disc membranes. It uses the energy from ATP binding and hydrolysis to transport N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine (N-Ret-PE), the Schiff base adduct of retinal and phosphatidylethanolamine, from the lumen to the cytoplasmic leaflet of disc membranes. This ensures that all-trans-retinal and excess 11-cis-retinal are efficiently cleared from photoreceptor cells thereby preventing the accumulation of toxic retinoid compounds. Loss-of-function mutations in the gene encoding ABCA4 cause autosomal recessive Stargardt macular degeneration, also known as Stargardt disease (STGD1), and related autosomal recessive retinopathies characterized by impaired central vision and an accumulation of lipofuscin and bis-retinoid compounds. High resolution structures of ABCA4 in its substrate and nucleotide free state and containing bound N-Ret-PE or ATP have been determined by cryo-electron microscopy providing insight into the molecular architecture of ABCA4 and mechanisms underlying substrate recognition and conformational changes induced by ATP binding. The expression and functional characterization of a large number of disease-causing missense ABCA4 variants have been determined. These studies have shed light into the molecular mechanisms underlying Stargardt disease and a classification that reliably predicts the effect of a specific missense mutation on the severity of the disease. They also provide a framework for developing rational therapeutic treatments for ABCA4-associated diseases.

records.title: Assessment and management of retinopathy of prematurity in the era of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF).
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Assessment and management of retinopathy of prematurity in the era of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF).
content.abstract: The incidence of retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) continues to rise due to the improved survival of very low birth weight infants in developed countries. This epidemic is also fueled by increased survival of preterm babies with variable use of oxygen and a lack of ROP awareness and screening services in resource-limited regions. Improvements in technology and a basic understanding of the disease pathophysiology have changed the way we screen and manage ROP, educate providers and patients, and improve ROP awareness. Advancements in imaging techniques, expansion of telemedicine services, and the potential for artificial intelligence-assisted ROP screening programs have created opportunities to improve ROP care in areas with a shortage of ophthalmologists trained in ROP. To address the gap in provider knowledge regarding ROP, the Global Education Network for Retinopathy of Prematurity (GEN-ROP) created a web-based tele-education training module that can be used to educate all providers involved in ROP, including non-physician ROP screeners. Over the past 50 years, the treatment of severe ROP has evolved from limited treatment modalities to cryotherapy and laser photocoagulation. More recently, there has been growing evidence to support the use of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) agents for the treatment of severe ROP. However, VEGF is known to be important in organogenesis and microvascular maintenance, and given that intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment can result in systemic VEGF suppression over a period of at least 1-12 weeks, there are concerns regarding adverse effects and long-term ocular and systemic developmental consequences of anti-VEGF therapy. Future research in ophthalmology to address the growing burden of ROP should focus on cost-effective fundus imaging devices, implementation of artificial intelligence platforms, updated treatment algorithms with optimal use of anti-VEGF and careful investigation of its long-term effects, and surgical options in advanced ROP. Addressing these unmet needs will aid the global effort against the ROP epidemic and optimize our understanding and treatment of this blinding disease.

records.title: A CONSENSUS ON RISK MITIGATION FOR BROLUCIZUMAB IN NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: Patient Selection, Evaluation, and Treatment.

content.title: A CONSENSUS ON RISK MITIGATION FOR BROLUCIZUMAB IN NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: Patient Selection, Evaluation, and Treatment.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Brolucizumab has high efficacy in retinal fluid resolution and provides the possibility for longer dosing intervals in the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration. However, brolucizumab has been associated with events of retinal vasculitis and retinal vascular occlusion typically in the presence of other signs of intraocular inflammation (IOI). The purpose of this report is to provide guidance on the use of brolucizumab for neovascular age-related macular degeneration to a global audience.

Methods

A literature review was conducted on adverse events related to IOI after administration of brolucizumab in eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

Results

Possible risk factors for IOI and retinal vascular occlusion after brolucizumab should be considered before administering brolucizumab. Patients who receive brolucizumab should be educated on the symptoms, signs, and time course of IOI after brolucizumab. Before each injection of brolucizumab, physicians should assess the eye for any signs of inflammation and not treat with brolucizumab if inflammation is detected. Treatment of IOI should be prompt and provided with particular attention to the posterior segment.

Conclusion

Careful patient selection, patient education, assessment for inflammation, and intensive treatment of possible inflammation are important when using brolucizumab in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

records.title: What Are the Dry Eye Questionnaires Available in the Scientific Literature Used for? A Scoping Review.

content.title: What Are the Dry Eye Questionnaires Available in the Scientific Literature Used for? A Scoping Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Dry eye disease (DED) is a frequent chronic ophthalmic condition. Its diagnosis includes tests and patient reported outcomes (PRO) questionnaires. Although many PRO dry eye questionnaires (PRO-DEQs) are available, they differ greatly from each other and not all have been validated. The purpose of this study was to retrieve the PRO-DEQs present in the scientific literature by performing a descriptive analysis of them and identifying those with known validity and reliability characteristics and to perform a descriptive analysis of the geographic area, year of publication, and characteristics of the target population of the clinical studies that have used validated PRO-DEQs.

Design

Scoping review of the literature.

Methods

Searches were conducted in PubMed to retrieve PRO-DEQs published up to July 2018 and written in English, French, Italian or Spanish.

Results

One thousand six hundred two records were identified and 973 were included in the final analysis. Of these, 56 provided information on the design and validation of PRO-DEQs and 49 PRO-DEQs were identified. Twenty-two PRO-DEQs were validated (17 original and 5 modified) and 27 had no associated design, validity, and reliability studies. Most of the validated PRO-DEQs were designed in English, the number of items varies from 1 to 57, the dimensions are generally not specified, and they are self-administered. The greatest use of validated PRO-DEQs in clinical studies has been in Asia since 2010, with the Ocular Surface Disease Index being the most used. These questionnaires have been used mostly in adults, retired professionals, and people with visual diseases to diagnose DED.

Conclusions

This study aims to encourage the use of validated PRO-DEQs to guarantee the quality of the results obtained and the comparability and replicability among studies.

records.title: The Pattern of Retinal Ganglion Cell Loss in Wolfram Syndrome is Distinct From Mitochondrial Optic Neuropathies.

content.title: The Pattern of Retinal Ganglion Cell Loss in Wolfram Syndrome is Distinct From Mitochondrial Optic Neuropathies.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To describe the clinical phenotype of a cohort of patients with Wolfram syndrome (WS), focusing on the pattern of optic atrophy correlated with brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) measurements, as compared with patients with OPA1-related dominant optic atrophy (DOA).

Design

Retrospective, comparative cohort study.

Methods

We reviewed 25 patients with WS and 33 age-matched patients affected by OPA1-related DOA. Ophthalmologic, neurologic, endocrinologic, and MRI data from patients with WS were retrospectively retrieved. Ophthalmologic data were compared with data from patients with OPA1-related DOA and further analyzed for age dependency dividing patients in age quartiles. In a subgroup of patients with WS, we correlated the structural damage assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT) with brain MRI morphologic measurements. Visual acuity (VA), visual field mean defect (MD), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), and ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness were assessed by OCT and MRI morphologic measurements of anterior and posterior visual pathways.

Results

Optic atrophy was present in 100% of patients with WS. VA, MD, and RNFL thickness loss were worse in patients with WS with a faster decline since early age as compared with patients with DOA, who displayed a more stable visual function over the years. Conversely, GCL sectors were overall thinner in patients with DOA since early age compared to patients with WS, in which GCL thickness started to decline later in life. The neuroradiologic subanalysis on 11 patients with WS exhibited bilateral thinning of the anterior optic pathway, especially the prechiasmatic optic nerves and optic tracts. Optic tract thinning was significantly correlated with GCL thickness but not with RNFL parameters.

Conclusions

Our results showed a generally more severe and diffuse degeneration of both anterior and posterior visual pathways in patients with WS, with fast deterioration of visual function and structural OCT parameters since early age. The pattern observed with OCT suggests that retinal ganglion cell axonal degeneration (ie, RNFL) precedes cellular body atrophy (ie, GCL) by about a decade. This differs substantially from DOA, in which a more stable visual function is evident with predominant early loss of GCL, indirectly supporting the lack of a primary mitochondrial dysfunction in patients with WS.

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology-in the form of Machine Learning (ML) models and other models specialized in image recognition and processing, such as Convolutional Neural Networks Visual Transformers (CNN-ViTs)-is increasingly being used in ophthalmology. This review summarizes the main AI applications for laser-assisted refractive surgery. Methods: A wide-ranging literature search on the PubMed and ISI Thompson Web of Science databases was conducted. Results: AI is an all-encompassing technological concept that refers to either specific applications of ML/CNN models, such as in keratoconus screening or diagnosis, or agentic/multimodal AI applications that process different data types using a variety of AI models. The most clinically established applications found were corneal ectasia and keratoconus screening, in which AI models can reliably exceed 95% diagnostic accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity; nomogram-derived laser ablation programming; optimization of ray-tracing calculations for ray-traced ablation profiles; patient screening and selection for refractive surgery; visual and refractive result prediction; assessment of postoperative corneal ectasia risk; detection of intraoperative complications; research on the laser coupling effect; and other applications such as monitoring eye rubbing behavior in corneal ectasia suspects. Thus, singular, specific applications of AI models have made the largest clinical contributions. These results must be interpreted with a comparison of internal versus external validation, calibration, and generalizability. Overall the technology is highly promising. Agentic/multimodal AI frameworks are currently being discussed, with pilot studies published and applicability proposed in the context of large, high-patient-volume clinical practices. The technological advent of SHAP force plot graphs and saliency maps has improved understanding of the factors that contribute mechanistically to AI model reasoning, leading to more informed clinical decisions or research applicability, such as in finding parameters or factors linked to postoperative ectasia. Conclusions: AI is already established in laser-assisted refractive surgery in the form of models specialized in data-intensive analysis. At present, the best-performing novel AI models originate from the domain of large or multi-hospital settings due to requirements for multiple latest-generation diagnostic devices, high-volume patient data, computing expertise, and resources. Future directions could include clinical standardization and trickle-down dissemination of the technology. Agentic/multimodal AI has the potential to benefit large clinical/patient settings or offer access to expert knowledge in smaller practice settings. Agentic/multimodal AI implementation is offset by challenges in complexity, the technological limitations of LLMs ("hallucinations"), and ethical and legislative factors.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolomics and Lipidomics for Drug Discovery and Development.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolomics and Lipidomics for Drug Discovery and Development.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics has advanced through three technological generations: chemometric and classical machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with large language models so far entering mainly at the edges. The metabolome and lipidome lie closest to drug action, yet they have been among the slowest omics layers to adopt modern artificial intelligence. This paradox arises from their downstream position, which leaves them without a closed molecular reference and without the standardized, readily modeled data available to the genome and transcriptome. This review examines what these methods contribute to drug discovery and development. We survey applications across the drug-development pipeline, from target identification and mechanism of action deconvolution, through the prediction of drug-induced toxicity, to pharmacometabolomics, in which pre-dose metabolic phenotypes inform patient stratification and dosing. Across these metabolomic and lipidomic applications, interpretable classical machine learning remains the dominant form of artificial intelligence. The newer deep-learning and foundation models have concentrated instead on compound annotation, the cross-cutting problem of assigning confident identities to spectra, yet successive generations have mitigated but not solved it. Beyond annotation confidence, batch effects, semi-quantification, and small-cohort overfitting also remain practical constraints. Overall, targeted, hypothesis-driven metabolomic and lipidomic studies can already support drug discovery when their inferences are restricted to confidently identified metabolites, whereas open, hypothesis-free discovery remains the frontier. Near-term progress will depend less on any single algorithm than on curated spectral resources, rigorous measurement, leakage-aware validation, and honest reporting of identification confidence.

records.title: Automated Structured Reporting of Neurodegenerative Imaging Markers Using Quantitative MRI and Large Language Models.

content.title: Automated Structured Reporting of Neurodegenerative Imaging Markers Using Quantitative MRI and Large Language Models.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

To evaluate the feasibility of a quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-to-structured reporting pipeline that integrates quantitative MRI software with large language models (LLMs) for structured drafting of neurodegenerative imaging markers and generating clinician-facing report conclusions.

Materials and methods

A total of 192 patients with 3D T1 and 2D or 3D FLAIR MRI images from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative database were randomly selected. A deep-learning model generated structured report findings based on nine indices related to brain atrophy, white matter hyperintensities, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) space abnormalities, and compared with neuroradiologist-generated reference reports. Four LLMs (GPT-OSS 20B, MedGemma 4B, Phi-3, and Llama 3.1 8B) generated clinician-facing conclusions from the structured findings. Generated conclusions were evaluated using a five-point Likert scale across four metrics (accuracy, relevance, clarity, and satisfaction). Output errors were assessed across four categories: language, omission, addition, and numeric errors.

Results

Structured report findings demonstrated high accuracy for CSF space analysis (77.6%-97.9%). Performance for ordinal visual scales was lower under strict matching (27.1%-57.8%) but improved with a one-grade tolerance (91.7%-97.4%). Among LLMs, GPT achieved the highest scores across most metrics (median score 5) and exhibited the lowest output error rates. Smaller models (Phi-3 and Llama 3.1 8B) showed overall lower performance, with more language, omission, and addition errors. MedGemma demonstrated intermediate performance, but the highest rate of numeric errors.

Conclusion

Our quantitative MRI-to-structured reporting pipeline, integrating quantitative MRI software with LLM-based conclusion generation, might be feasible for automated structured drafting of neurodegenerative imaging markers.

records.title: Histopathological Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for Cancer Diagnosis and Gleason Grading: A Brief Review of Prostate Cancer.
records.publisher: Journal of clinical practice and research

content.title: Histopathological Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for Cancer Diagnosis and Gleason Grading: A Brief Review of Prostate Cancer.
content.abstract:
Objective

Prostate cancer, one of the most common cancers affecting men's health worldwide, ranks second among cancer-related deaths. Therefore, it represents a critical health issue, and early diagnosis is crucial. Several imaging and analytical methods are used to diagnose this condition.

Materials and methods

This study focuses on research conducted between 2021 and 2025 that analyzes, diagnoses, and grades prostate cancer based on histopathological images using machine learning and deep learning algorithms. In this context, the reviewed studies also include an analysis of findings related to preprocessing and feature extraction methods that may aid in prostate cancer detection, as well as the classifiers used.

Results

According to the findings of the reviewed studies, artificial intelligence-supported prostate cancer detection systems demonstrate high clinical performance and significantly improve the diagnostic accuracy of pathologists by enabling rapid diagnosis. The presented research findings indicate a need for comprehensive studies focusing on prostate cancer using histopathological images.

Conclusion

The integration of artificial intelligence is transforming prostate cancer pathology from a traditional and subjective process into a data-driven and standardized framework. This systematic analysis of histopathological images will make significant contributions to future prostate cancer research, help achieve more reliable results in clinical decision-making processes, and lay the groundwork for personalized medicine.

records.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.

content.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

records.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study.

content.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study.
content.abstract:
Background

Spirometry is one of the most used pulmonary function tests for assessing respiratory function and diagnosing ventilatory disorders in clinical practice. Evaluation of test validity and interpretation is typically performed by trained healthcare professionals. The present study aims to evaluate the capability of a publicly available large language model (LLM) to perform quality assurance and interpretations of spirometry tests.

Methods

A total of 150 spirometry tests were retrospectively collected from the pulmonary function laboratories. The spirometry tests were evaluated for acceptability and interpreted by clinicians according to ATS/ERS recommendations as part of standard clinical practice. Subsequently, a publicly available LLM (ChatGPT 5.5) was prompted to evaluate the acceptability and interpret the same spirometry tests according to ATS/ERS criteria. The model interpreted each spirometry test on three separate occasions for assessing reproducibility. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were calculated by comparing LLM assessments with clinician assessments of spirometry test acceptability and interpretation.

Results

For spirometry acceptability evaluation, ChatGPT demonstrated an overall accuracy of 87% (95% CI: 81%-92%), sensitivity of 91% (95% CI: 85%-95%), specificity of 61% (95% CI 39%-80%), PPV of 94% (95% CI: 89%-97%), and NPV of 48(95% CI: 29%-67%) with Cohen's k of 0.46. The spiromteric interpretation agreement with the clinicians reference standard was moderate, with exact agreement of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.54-0.69) while Cohen's Kappa (Unweighted) was 0.47 (95% CI: 0.37-0.56) and Macro F1 score was 0.39 (95% CI: 0.33-0.49). Reproducibility across three independent trials was moderate (Fleiss' κ 0.58). Class-specific interpretation performance varied by category; sensitivity was highest for normal pattern and restrictive defects (0.72), whereas sensitivity for obstructive defects was 0.27. F1-scores were highest for normal and restrictive defects (0.81 and 0.62, respectively).

Conclusion

The current findings suggest that ChatGPT 5.5 has a limited capability, at its current stage of development, to serve as a reliable tool for independent spirometry interpretation in clinical practice. Nevertheless, it may serve as an adjunct to clinical decision-making and educational tools. Prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Chatbots in University Level Dental Education: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Chatbots in University Level Dental Education: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI), mainly AI-driven chatbots and large language models (LLMs) is reshaping dental education through adaptive, interactive, and simulation-based learning. While the transition in technology has been rapid, the evidence about the educational effectiveness of these technologies is still very diverse and not entirely directed.

Aim

To analyze the roles, educational effectiveness, and impact of integrating AI-driven chatbots and LLMs in dental education at the university level with a focus on learning outcomes and implementation practices.

Methods

The researchers conducted a thorough search of the electronic databases PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase for articles published from January 2018 to November 2025. This review met the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 criteria and was made up of original research articles on dental studentsand educators who were using AI-based chatbots as interventions. The outcomes measured were knowledge gain, clinical reasoning, diagnostic accuracy, communication skills, and engagement of learners. Due to the differences in the methodologies used the authors opted for a narrative synthesis approach.

Results

Six studies met the eligibility criteria and showed potential benefits of AI-driven chatbots and LLMs for diagnostic reasoning, learning performance, engagement, and individualized feedback although methodological and outcome heterogeneity limited direct comparison.

Conclusion

AI-driven chatbots and LLMs may complement university-level dental education, but their effectiveness and safe implementation require further rigorous evaluation.

records.title: Advancing Cancer Biomarker Discovery Through Multi-Omics, Bioinformatics, and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Advancing Cancer Biomarker Discovery Through Multi-Omics, Bioinformatics, and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract: The rapid accumulation of multi-omics data provides increasing opportunities for cancer biomarker discovery, but the heterogeneity and high dimensionality of these datasets remain major challenges for data integration and analysis. This review examines the application of bioinformatics and artificial intelligence for multi-omics integration in cancer biomarker research. Common multi-omics data paradigms and integration strategies are discussed, followed by a review of the bioinformatics, machine learning and deep learning approaches applied across 84 included studies. Cross-study comparison showed limited recurrence among the reported biomarkers, with only 15 biomarkers identified in at least four studies. Further assessment of the 13 recurrent protein-coding biomarkers showed significant protein-protein interaction enrichment and functional convergence in cancer-related processes, particularly PI3K/AKT and ERBB2-related signaling. This review also highlights current challenges, including missing data, heterogeneity across datasets, limited independent validation and the interpretability of artificial intelligence models. Future research may benefit from integrating multi-omics data with clinical information, pathological imaging, electronic health records, single-cell multi-omics and radiomics, together with broader datasets and greater use of independent validation to support the translation of multi-omics biomarker findings into clinical applications.

records.title: Comparative analysis and optimization of multi-model artificial intelligence for microscopic detection of fungal structures in superficial fungal infections.
records.publisher: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

content.title: Comparative analysis and optimization of multi-model artificial intelligence for microscopic detection of fungal structures in superficial fungal infections.
content.abstract:
Background

Superficial fungal infections present a growing threat to global public health. Traditional diagnostic techniques, including microscopy and culture, are time-consuming and subjective, often limiting diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic tools offer a promising adjunct to improve efficiency and standardization of microscopic fungal detection.

Methods

We systematically compared six deep learning models, including the You Only Look Once (YOLO) series, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) series and the Detection Transformer (DETR). Three evaluation datasets were constructed. Datasets 1 and 2 (derived from 4000 hyphae and 4500 spore images) were used to assess image-level detection using sensitivity, precision and F1 score. Dataset 1 was manually annotated for the YOLO series and DETR; Dataset 2 (unannotated) served as the CNN series' benchmark. Dataset 3 (1, 870 specimens from 1, 730 patients) was used to evaluate sample-level performance via confusion matrix analysis for the YOLO series and DETR models, employing medical records as the reference standard. The best-performing model was optimized and deployed into an online auxiliary diagnostic platform for real-time clinical decision support.

Results

YOLOv11 outperformed all other evaluated architectures. Detection was generally better at 400× than at 200× magnification. Notably, the F1 score for hyphae detection by YOLOv11 increased from 90.42% (200×) to 92.06% (400×). All models achieved higher accuracy for spores than hyphae. Patient-level confusion-matrix analysis confirmed YOLOv11 superiority. After optimizing an Intersection over Union (IoU) threshold of 0.25 and the maximum confidence (Cmax) strategy, 200× hyphae F1 rose to 97.84% and the positive predictive value (PPV) to 98.27%. Subgroup analysis showed robust performance across different diseases, with tinea capitis reaching the highest F1 score (98.53%).

Conclusion

The optimized YOLOv11 model demonstrates potential as a rapid and standardized supportive tool for the microscopic detection of fungal structures in superficial fungal infections. Integration into an online auxiliary diagnostic platform demonstrates the feasibility of real-time AI-assisted fungal detection, offering a standardized tool to support clinical decision-making. This work supports AI as a potential complement to clinical and laboratory expertise, pending further validation in prospective and multi-center settings, and highlights its potential to streamline fungal infection diagnostic workflows.

records.title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.

content.title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has drastically enhanced healthcare diagnostics with automated disease detection, predictive analytics, and intelligent systems for clinical decision support. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning models hampers interpretability, clinical trust, and regulatory acceptance and raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity. This paper presents comprehensive experimental frameworks for developing and evaluating explainable AI models for secure healthcare diagnostics. The suggested model combines responsible data management, multimodal preprocessing, secure deep learning models, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, and reproducible validation procedures in a single healthcare diagnostic pipeline. Methods of explaining, such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual analysis, were used to make the models more transparent and understandable for clinicians. At the same time, federated learning and differential privacy methods were used to securely manage highly sensitive patient data. Experimental evaluation has shown 96% classification accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 95% specificity. These results were consistent in heterogeneous healthcare datasets. Compared to traditional black-box models, the explainability framework not only enhanced the interpretability of the results but also more accurately identified the regions relevant for diagnosis. Moreover, the secure federated learning architecture minimized privacy leakages without sacrificing the predictive performance and remained robust even when exposed to adversarial perturbations. An external evaluation also confirmed the reproducibility and generalizability of the protocols involved. This methodology offers a comprehensive and reliable foundation for deploying AI-powered diagnostics across multiple healthcare domains: radiology, pathology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and precision medicine.

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic detection of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but available studies address distinct diagnostic questions. We systematically reviewed studies evaluating AI-based STEMI detection from 12-lead electrocardiograms and separately synthesized AI performance against a clinical reference standard, AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, and AI agreement with physician electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 2010 through March 10, 2025. Bivariate random-effects models generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC). Twenty-six studies comprising 539,876 ECGs were included. In 20 studies comparing AI with a clinical reference standard, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.91-0.97), specificity 0.95 (0.90-0.98), AUC 0.98 (0.97-0.99), positive likelihood ratio 19.2 (9.3-39.5), and negative likelihood ratio 0.05 (0.03-0.10).
